summary: Cleveland NF tower site, San Diego Co.: CCC lookout built 1935, replaced 1965, heavily damaged in a 1988 Marine helicopter collision and removed.

facts.design: 1935: 30-ft steel K-brace tower with 14x14-ft live-in wood cab (CCC); 1965: 30-ft steel tower with 13x13-ft steel CL-104 cab
facts.status_note: The 1965 tower was heavily damaged in a 1988 collision with a Marine helicopter and removed.

events.note: Built by the Civilian Conservation Corps: 30-ft steel K-brace tower with a 14x14-ft live-in wood cab.
A lookout is named in a 1938 California Ranger item quoted on Forest Lookouts.
Replaced by a Forest Service standard CL-104 lookout: 30-ft steel tower with a 13x13-ft steel cab.
Devil's Canyon fire surrounded the tower and burned a garage. Per a Eugene Register-Guard report quoted on Forest Lookouts, the tower did not burn.
The 1965 lookout was burned over in a wildfire.
On March 2, 1988 a Marine CH-46E helicopter collided with the tower. The San Diego chapter says it was destroyed; Forest Lookouts says it was heavily damaged and had to be removed.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The San Diego chapter says the 1965 tower was destroyed in the 1988 collision. The Forest Lookouts page says it was heavily damaged and had to be removed. Both agree the 1965 tower did not survive the collision.
The register and the San Diego chapter both say the lookout was known as both Santa Margarita and Margarita Peak Lookout, which explains the two names in the record.

notes_for_editor: Elevation conflict: the register gives 2,502 ft (763 m), which matches the 762.6 m in our record, while the San Diego chapter gives 3,189 ft (972 m). Coordinates: the record's point (33.45678, -117.39739) matches the firelookout.org list; the register gives N 33.444420, W 117.383330, about 1.9 km away. Not proposed as a correction, because two sources agree on the record's point. A firelookout.org California list has a Santa Margarita entry with NHLR US 1328, CA 151 and the record's coordinates. Grep context near it shows 'Standing' and '3-Story Cab' lines, but we could not confirm those belong to this entry, and we did not read its register page. This conflicts with the removal reported elsewhere and needs a human check. The 1988 loss rests on the Forest Lookouts and San Diego chapter pages; no source gives current site access or remains, and the register's site video links were not viewed. No WebSearch was available in this run. Fetch budget for this lookout was used up.
